subject: HealthLytics — security questionnaire and next steps
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Barnes <obarnes@healthlytics.com>, Dr. Simon Reyes <simon.reyes@healthlytics.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Apr 2025 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: HealthLytics — security questionnaire and next steps

Hi Olivia / Simon — thanks again for the demo and the call today. Quick recap + proposed next steps on the security/compliance side so we can align our teams.

Call recap (security topics):
- SOC 2: you mentioned audit work starting later this year and an existing controls program. Please confirm if you expect Type II by Q4 2025 or earlier.
- Data residency & hosting: GCP (us-central) is primary; you said EU zones are planned for 2025 — confirm region(s) that will hold PHI.
- HIPAA: you indicated some workflows will process PHI and will need a BAA.
- Host-level controls: encryption at rest, KMS usage, key rotation cadence and access controls are the items we'll ask about in the questionnaire.

What we propose (recommended path):
1) SIG Enterprise questionnaire (full) as the primary form — most efficient for enterprise procurement and maps to CAIQ where needed.
2) Prefill: our security team (with a little help from your technical contact) can prefill known items to keep the lift low for you.
3) Evidence handoff: request network diagram, SOC 2 report when available, sample encryption config screenshots, and a list of infra owners.

Clarifying questions for you to confirm:
- Which questionnaire do you prefer to start with: SIG (recommended) or a CAIQ/custom RFI?
- Primary technical contact for evidence collection (name + email + timezone).
- Is PHI currently stored in us-central only or mirrored to EU?
- Any non-production systems that must be excluded from the scope?

Timeline proposal:
- Let us know preference and contact today or tomorrow.
- If SIG -> we can send prefill template within 24 hours and aim for a first-pass prefill in 5 business days after we have the contact and access to basic artifacts.

Attachments: redwood-sig-intake-guide.pdf (quick explanation of our SIG workflow and evidence checklist).

Next steps: please reply with the questionnaire preference and primary technical contact. If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute evidence-handoff call.

Thanks,
Chloe Martin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0193

Thanks Chloe — great recap. A few answers and a couple of asks from our side.

Answers:
- SOC 2: we are in the middle of a controls maturity project; target is SOC 2 Type II with a readiness assessment in June and a formal audit kickoff in late Q3 (aim for report in Q4 2025). I'll put a short note in the ticket about current evidence availability.
- Hosting/Residency: primary production is GCP us-central; we are piloting EU-west for non-production today and plan to expand EU production later this year — for PHI we currently have it in us-central only.
- HIPAA: yes, we handle PHI for a subset of workflows — we will need a BAA.

Questions for Redwood:
1) Would you prefer we complete the full SIG first or a CAIQ as a lower-effort starting point? Which gives you the most confidence for a procurement review?
2) Does Redwood have a standard BAA we can review, or do you prefer DocuSign exchange of our standard?

I've attached our initial RFI spreadsheet to help scope (HealthLytics_Security_RFI_v1.xlsx). Our technical lead for this scope is:
- Name: Michael Tanaka (Engineering Manager)
- Email: mtanaka@healthlytics.com
- TZ: PDT (San Francisco)

We can do a 30-minute handoff call next week if that helps.

Best,
Olivia Barnes
Head of Procurement | HealthLytics
obarnes@healthlytics.com

Hi Olivia / Michael — thanks for the quick responses and for sharing Michael as the technical lead. Short answers to your questions and a next-step plan below.

1) Questionnaire approach: we recommend the SIG Enterprise (full) for enterprise procurement — it provides the best mapping to customer controls and is what most of our larger customers expect. If you'd prefer a phased approach we can start with a CAIQ-lite and move to full SIG, but that often extends procurement time.

2) BAA: Redwood has a standard BAA template we can share. I can send via DocuSign or you can share yours first; whichever you prefer. The legal team usually reviews counterparty BAAs but sharing ours will speed execution in most cases.

3) Evidence we will request (initial):
- Current SOC 2 readiness notes and any prior Type I reports (if applicable)
- Network diagram (VPC/subnet diagram) and dataflow for PHI
- KMS configuration screenshots or architecture note showing key management and rotation
- Encryption at rest description and TLS termination point (load balancer vs host)
- List of services in-scope and any third-party subprocessors

Attached: redwood-sig-prefill-template.xlsx — if Michael or your SRE can drop a few items into this sheet we'll prefill the SIG and highlight outstanding evidence items to minimize back-and-forth.

Suggested schedule:
- Today: confirm SIG vs CAIQ and Michael as tech lead (done).
- By Fri (2 business days): Michael fills top-line prefill fields (or we can run through on a 30-min call).
- Week of Apr 21: Redwood security team reviews, sends back evidence checklist and follow-up questions.

If it's helpful I can schedule a 30-minute evidence handoff with Michael and our security engineer (Marissa). Do you have 30 minutes on Mon Apr 14 or Tue Apr 15?

Thanks,
Chloe
